Auto follows your device\'s own setting, and the choice stays on this device.
Press and hold, then drift to where you stand.
One slider per side of the opinion.
A tap always adds a small positive one. This is what a longer press opens, everywhere.
Ask first when one submit signs more than one action.
Every signed action is paid for separately. A post\'s license is settled when it is first signed and never changes.
The number pairs behind the faces.
Every feed starts from what it shows, and a change made inside a feed lasts until you change it back. Both choices stay on this device.
Hiding someone clears your own feed of them. Nothing changes for them, and their profile still opens if you go looking.
Off, the veil stays until you tap it.
On, sensitive content stands unveiled wherever you read.
This choice follows your account to every device.
Your key signs everything you publish and lives only in this app. Your recovery code is the only way back.
Your key signs everything you publish and lives only in this app. Until you make a recovery code, it can\'t be brought back.
A device you sign out can stay signed in for up to 15 minutes.
Changing your password signs out every other device.
Don\'t remember this account on this device
Your key, your draft and any kept picks are cleared from this app when you sign out.
Nothing is deleted here. The next screen says what goes and what stays, and the deletion is confirmed by a link we email you.
Nothing is deleted here. The next screen says what goes and what stays.
You can delete your account once your registration lands.
Canceled — your account stays, and nothing was deleted.
This takes your name off CoGra. What you signed stays on the graph, because it is other people\'s record as much as yours — what goes is everything that says it was you.
Nothing has landed yet — deleting removes your application and your account right away.
Your profile — display name, bio and picture.
The link between you and this account. Nothing left here points back to you.
Your sessions, and what this account kept for you alone: saved items, hidden accounts, what you have read.
Everything you signed, and everything others signed about you. Your posts still route and still credit their author; what is removed leaves a mark saying so.
The words and pictures go out of your posts and comments, each leaving its mark. Leave this off and they stay as you wrote them.
Nothing is deleted until you open that link. After that it runs in seven days, and you can cancel from any device until it does.
We sent a link to %1$s. Opening it confirms the deletion and starts the seven days.
Until you open it nothing is scheduled and nothing has changed. Closing this screen changes nothing either — the link is the whole of it.
Sent again — the link is on its way to %1$s.
Your account is deleted in %1$s, on %2$s. Until then nothing has changed, and canceling keeps everything as it is.
Your account and everything you posted are deleted in %1$s
That\'s %1$s. Until then nothing changes, and you can cancel from any device.
Added — what you posted goes too.
You\'re not signed in here, and you don\'t need to be — the link was the proof.
It may have been used already, or a newer request replaced it. If you still mean to delete your account, ask again from settings.

Your key lives only in this app. Clear the app\'s data, or uninstall it without keeping the data, and the key is erased with it — without your recovery code, your account is gone for good. Your draft, any kept picks and the choices kept on this device go too, and you\'re signed out. What you\'ve seen comes back when you sign in.

Your key lives only in this app, and it has no recovery code yet. Clear the app\'s data, or uninstall it without keeping the data, and the key is erased with it — your account is gone for good. Your draft, any kept picks and the choices kept on this device go too, and you\'re signed out. What you\'ve seen comes back when you sign in.

This app holds the only copy of your key, and it has no recovery code. Erase everything and your account is gone for good — no one, including CoGra, can bring it back. Your draft, any kept picks and the choices kept on this device go too, and you\'re signed out.

Your key is erased with everything else, and only your recovery code can bring it back — without the code, your account is gone for good. Your draft, any kept picks and the choices kept on this device go too, and you\'re signed out. What you\'ve seen comes back when you sign in.

This app holds the only copy of your key. Signing out leaves your key, your draft and any opinions you kept pending here, locked until you sign in again. Erase them instead, and no one — including CoGra — can bring them back.
Where every new post starts. A post\'s terms settle when it is first signed, so changing this never reaches one you have already published.
Changing your password signs out every other device. This one stays signed in.
Your current password is asked for even though you are signed in: a live session is not proof enough to change the credential behind it.
Password changed — other devices are signed out.
A password is at least 12 characters.
A password is at most 128 characters.
That password has turned up in a data breach — pick another one.
\@%1$s is how people mention and find you. Everything you have published stays yours — the handle is a name, not the account.
3 to 30 characters: letters, numbers and underscore. Handles are always lowercase.
Links to your old handle stop working the moment you change it, and anyone can claim it afterwards.
Links to \@%1$s stop working the moment it changes, and anyone can claim \@%1$s afterwards.
Your email signs you in, and it is the only way back if you lose your password — so a change is proved from both ends.
Waiting for a new email and your password
A code goes to %1$s and a link to the new address. Your email is unchanged until both have been answered.
That doesn\'t look like an email address.
Your email isn\'t verified yet, so the new address is all a change needs. A fresh link goes there, and the one sent to %1$s stops working.
Sent — the link is on its way to %1$s.
Two messages, two different errands — a code to type here, and a link to open at the new address. Your email moves when both have been answered, in either order.
Until both sides land your account keeps the address it has, and a reset still goes there.
Done on this side — now open the link at %1$s
Too many tries — for safety we have disabled your current code. Resend sends a fresh one.
This change ran out before both sides landed. Your email stays as it is — start again from settings.
That address now belongs to another account. Your email stays as it is — if the address frees up before the change runs out, confirming again applies it.
Sent again — the code is on its way to %1$s.
Sent again — the link is on its way to %1$s.
One side left: the code we sent to %1$s. Your email moves once it\'s typed in.
You sign in with %1$s from now on, and resets go there too.
The change it belonged to was canceled. Your email is still %1$s.
The change it belonged to already happened. Your email is now %1$s.
The change it belonged to ran out before both sides landed. Your email is still %1$s.
This link isn\'t for this account
It confirms a new address for another account, so nothing changed here. Open it signed in as that account to finish the change.
Sign in to finish the change
This link confirms %1$s as your new address. It counts once you\'re signed in.
The change it belonged to may have run out, been canceled or already happened — this link can\'t move your email anymore.
It isn\'t a link CoGra knows — it may be mistyped, or from a change long gone. Your email stays as it is.
Create or replace your recovery code. A new code re-encrypts your key and replaces the old backup — recovery always uses the newest one.
Your actor key isn\'t on this phone, so there\'s nothing to back up. Restore it first from the home screen.
Write this code down somewhere safe. It is shown only this once; any older code stops working.
Can\'t reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
Unlock to create a new recovery code
With no screen lock or fingerprint, anyone holding this phone can reveal or replace your key. Set a lock up first — or continue if you\'re sure this phone is safe.

This key is what signs everything you publish, and it lives only on this phone. Write it down or store it somewhere safe and you keep it whatever happens to CoGra. Anyone who has a copy can act as you.
This phone doesn\'t hold your key. Restore it first from the home screen.
